title: Pointwise limits of marked sections of a cocartesian fibration
statement: Use the quasicategories, coherent functors and limits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], in fixed nested universes. Let $p:E\to S$ be a cocartesian fibration of quasicategories, $g:T\to S$ a functor with $T$ small, $J$ a small simplicial set, and $W$ a set of edges of $T$. Write $\operatorname{Sect}_W(g^*E)$ for the full infinity subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}_S(T,E)$ consisting of functors carrying each edge in $W$ to a $p$-cocartesian edge. Suppose every fiber $E_{g(t)}$ admits $J$-indexed limits and, for each $w:t\to t'$ in $W$, its transport $g(w)_!:E_{g(t)}\to E_{g(t')}$ preserves those limits. Then $\operatorname{Fun}_S(T,E)$ admits $J$-indexed limits computed in the fibers, and $\operatorname{Sect}_W(g^*E)$ is closed under them. Evaluation at all vertices of $T$ jointly detects limit cones in this full subcategory. Equivalently its inclusion creates these limits. No preservation of limits by transports on unmarked arrows is assumed. The empty shape $J=\varnothing$ is included.

source.place: Agent-formulated marked-section theorem underlying Section 3.2.2, especially the proof of Proposition 3.2.2.1 and Corollaries 3.2.2.3-3.2.2.5, printed pp.357-364; not a direct application of their symmetric-operad statements. It is the general relative-limit/relative right Kan extension argument for a cocartesian fibration, using HTT Proposition 4.3.1.10 and Corollary 4.3.1.11. Report.md gives the argument and makes explicit why it is independent of symmetry. Read from retained sandbox source; full shared archive WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text:
Pull back to $q:X=T\times_SE\to T$, and put $\Gamma=\operatorname{Fun}_T(T,X)=\operatorname{Fun}_S(T,E)$. Inner-horn fillers and cocartesian lifts for $q$ are obtained by using those for $p$ and retaining the prescribed $T$-coordinate, so $q$ is a cocartesian fibration and $X$ is a quasicategory. The fiber is $X_t=E_{g(t)}$. Use [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] to pass between the horn and mapping-space conventions before applying [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport]. That theorem gives a cocartesian fibration $q_J:\operatorname{Fun}(J,X)\to\operatorname{Fun}(J,T)$. Pull it back along the constant-diagram functor $\Delta_J:T\to\operatorname{Fun}(J,T)$, obtaining
$$d:D=T\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,T)}\operatorname{Fun}(J,X)\longrightarrow T.$$
Again the same relative horn fillers and lifts prove this is a cocartesian fibration, with fiber $D_t=\operatorname{Fun}(J,X_t)$ and transport $\operatorname{Fun}(J,w_!)$. The relative diagonal $F:X\to D$ sends $x$ to its constant $J$-diagram. A cocartesian edge is sent to a transformation with cocartesian components, so $F$ preserves cocartesian edges by the pointwise theorem. Applying that theorem also with shape $T$ shows that $\Gamma$ is a quasicategory, being the strict fiber over $1_T$ of an inner fibration between quasicategories. Currying is the degreewise identity on maps $J\times T\times\Delta^n\to X$ over $T$ and identifies $\operatorname{Fun}_T(T,D)$ with $\operatorname{Fun}(J,\Gamma)$. No limit preservation by a transport is used here.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.2.1, cocartesian dual; construction by pullback and simplicial currying

proof.text:
For each vertex $t$, every diagram $B:J\to X_t$ has a limit cone $\epsilon_B:\Delta_J l_B\to B$ by hypothesis. The cone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] says precisely that
$$\operatorname{Map}_{X_t}(x,l_B)\xrightarrow{\epsilon_B\circ\Delta_J(-)}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,X_t)}(\Delta_Jx,B)$$
is an equivalence for every $x$. Apply [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] to $\Delta_J:X_t\to D_t$ and the whole full subcategory $D_t$. It assembles these universal arrows into a coherent right adjoint $R_t$ and counit. Thus the fiber adjunctions needed below exist without postulating functorial choices of fiber limits. Their units are the adjuncts of identities; the universal-arrow equivalences identify the two unit/counit composites with identities and supply the triangle homotopies.

source.place: Section 7.3.2: fiberwise adjunction input; agent application of universal arrows to the diagonal

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-cocartesian-relative-right-adjoint] to $F:X\to D$ over $T$. Both maps to $T$ are cocartesian fibrations, $F$ preserves their cocartesian edges by step 1, and its fiber right adjoints are supplied by step 2. Obtain $R:D\to X$ with unit $\eta$ and counit $\epsilon$ and triangle homotopies, all over $1_T$. Postcomposition therefore gives functors $F_*:\Gamma\to\operatorname{Fun}_T(T,D)$ and $R_*$ in the reverse direction, with the same sectionwise unit, counit and homotopies. The maps on section mapping spaces are explicitly $a\mapsto R_*(a)\eta_A$ and $b\mapsto\epsilon_B F_*(b)$. Naturality and the two triangle homotopies show that these composites are homotopic to the identities, using the associative/unital mapping-space composition of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Thus they are inverse equivalences. Under currying, $F_*$ is $\Delta_J:\Gamma\to\operatorname{Fun}(J,\Gamma)$. For $B:J\to\Gamma$, let $\widetilde B:T\to D$ be its curried section and put $L=R\widetilde B$. The counit gives a cone $\lambda:\Delta_JL\to B$; the section mapping-space equivalence and [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] make it a limit cone in $\Gamma$. On evaluation at $t$, it is the counit of the fiber adjunction, hence a limit cone on $B_t$ in $X_t$.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.2.6, cocartesian/right-adjoint dual, and Proposition 7.3.2.5; explicit restriction of the adjunction to sections

proof.text: Evaluation at vertices detects equivalence edges of $\Gamma$. Indeed a section transformation $u$ with equivalence components is an equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(T,X)$ by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. For the inner fibration $q_T:\operatorname{Fun}(T,X)\to\operatorname{Fun}(T,T)$ from [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport], its base edge is the identity at $1_T$. Precomposition with $u$ is an equivalence on mapping spaces (compose with an inverse, using [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]), and precomposition with its base identity is an equivalence. The square in [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] is consequently a homotopy pullback, so $u$ is $q_T$-cocartesian. Its initial-outer-horn fillers over the constant simplex at $1_T$ are fillers inside the fiber $\Gamma$. The converse outer-horn criterion [lem-cbc-equivalence-outer-horn-filling] makes $u$ an equivalence in $\Gamma$ itself. The reverse implication follows by evaluating its inverse and its two inverse triangles.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3, dual, and the equivalence outer-horn criterion; elementary application to the strict section fiber

proof.text: For any other cone $\mu:\Delta_J A\to B$ in $\Gamma$, the limiting cone $\lambda$ of step 3 provides a comparison $u:A\to L$ together with a coherent identification $\lambda\Delta_Ju\simeq\mu$. If every $\mu_t$ is limiting, then $u_t$ is an equivalence: it is a morphism between terminal objects in the fiber cone category, whose terminal-object subcategory is a contractible Kan complex by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Step 4 makes $u$ an equivalence of sections. The induced equivalence of cones makes $\mu$ limiting, since its cone mapping spaces are identified with those of $\lambda$. Conversely, if $\mu$ is limiting, contractibility of the terminal-object subcategory of the cone category gives an equivalence of cones $\mu\simeq\lambda$; evaluating that equivalence shows that each $\mu_t$ is limiting. Hence a cone in $\Gamma$ is limiting if and only if its vertex evaluations are limiting.

source.place: Section 3.2.2, pointwise-limit criterion; agent deduction from the section adjunction and uniqueness of limits

proof.text:
Now let $B:J\to\operatorname{Sect}_W(g^*E)$ and take the cone $\lambda$ just constructed in $\Gamma$. Fix $w:t\to t'$ in $W$ and write $w_!$ for $g(w)_!$. The restriction of $B$ to this edge is a coherent transformation covering $g(w)$; [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] factors it through its cocartesian transport, giving
$$\theta:w_!B_t\longrightarrow B_{t'}.$$
For every vertex $j$ of $J$, the edge $B_j(w)$ is $p$-cocartesian by the marking condition. Its factorization through a chosen cocartesian lift has an equivalence as its vertical comparison: the two cocartesian lifts are initial in the lift category of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality], and the universal comparison of their targets is an equivalence in $E_{g(t')}$. Thus all components of $\theta$ are equivalences, and [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes $\theta$ an equivalence of $J$-diagrams. By the hypothesis on this marked edge, $w_!\lambda_t$ is a limit cone on $w_!B_t$. Postcompose with $\theta$ to obtain a limit cone on $B_{t'}$ with apex $w_!L(t)$: in the cone mapping-space criterion, postcomposition with the diagram equivalence identifies the right sides, so universality is retained. This uses preservation only for the chosen $w\in W$.

source.place: Section 3.2.2: inert-edge check, abstracted to a marked edge; componentwise cocartesian transport and the stated preservation hypothesis

proof.text:
Factor the edge $L(w)$ through a chosen $p$-cocartesian lift $c:L(t)\to w_!L(t)$, writing the vertical comparison as $v:w_!L(t)\to L(t')$ with a coherent triangle $L(w)\simeq vc$. Existence with its coherent data is the mapping-fiber assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport], also applied to the cone diagram; its compatibility with precomposition identifies the induced map of cones with
$$\bigl(w_!L(t),\theta\circ w_!\lambda_t\bigr)\longrightarrow\bigl(L(t'),\lambda_{t'}\bigr).$$
This is exactly the naturality square of the section cone $\lambda$ on $w$, including its $J$-coherences. Both cones are limiting by step 6 and step 3. Their comparison is an equivalence of cones by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], hence $v$ is an equivalence in the fiber. An equivalence over an identity is $p$-cocartesian by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]: both horizontal precomposition maps in its square are equivalences. The cocartesian cancellation/composition clause of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] applied to $c,v,L(w)$ proves that $L(w)$ is $p$-cocartesian. Thus $L$ lies in the marked full subcategory. The same reasoning applies to any pointwise limiting cone on $B$, not merely the chosen cone.

source.place: Section 3.2.2: marked-arrow preservation; explicit universal cone comparison rather than an assumed commuting transport

proof.text: Because the marked category is full in $\Gamma$, its cone category on $B$ is the full subcategory of the ambient cone category on cones with marked apex. The ambient limiting cone $\lambda$ has marked apex by step 7, so its mapping spaces from these cones remain contractible; it is limiting in the marked category. If a marked cone has limiting evaluations, step 5 makes it ambient limiting and hence marked limiting. Conversely, a cone limiting in the marked category is equivalent there to $\lambda$, by the terminal-object assertion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]; evaluation of this equivalence makes all its evaluations limiting. Finally any ambient limiting cone on $B$ is pointwise limiting by step 5, and step 7 makes its apex marked. Fullness retains every transformation and higher simplex of its universal property. Therefore inclusion creates these limits, with the usual contractible choice of a lift, and evaluation jointly detects them. When $J=\varnothing$, $D_t=\operatorname{Fun}(\varnothing,X_t)=*$ and $R_t$ selects the terminal object supplied by the hypothesis; steps 1-7 still apply, and step 6 uses preservation of terminal objects exactly on marked edges. When $T=\varnothing$, the section category is $*$ and the evaluation criterion is vacuous and valid. No weak-contractibility assumption on $J$ and no preservation assumption on unmarked transports entered any step.

source.place: Corollaries 3.2.2.3-3.2.2.5: full-subcategory limit conclusion, with arbitrary markings and the empty shape checked directly

I checked the direction of variance on S=T=Delta^1: for a cocartesian fibration, limits of sections are computed pointwise with no preservation by the transport, and preservation is needed exactly on marked edges. I also checked J empty, T empty and the worker's example where the transport is constant at 0, which does not preserve the terminal object. Each step uses what its cited node states. Step 1 converts between the horn and mapping-space notions of cocartesian with the mapping criterion, and the diagonal preserves cocartesian edges because those are componentwise. In step 3, the relative right adjoint (the opposite of HA 7.3.2.6) needs cocartesian fibrations, a functor preserving cocartesian edges and fiber right adjoints, and nothing more. Step 4 shows that pointwise equivalences are equivalences in the section fiber, by cocartesian-over-identity plus the converse outer-horn criterion. It is marked elementary although it combines five cited statements, which is borderline but every input is cited. Steps 6-7 use preservation only for w in W, then the equivalence of the target comparison and the 2-out-of-3 clause of composition-initiality. Searching dag/nodes found no duplicate (the Yoneda presheaf limits, relative colimit completion and section-colimit nodes all state something else). The graph has no cycle and no SGA source is cited.
